companyRankingLists.description: Creating a more empathetic workplace looks like staying loyal to workers, emphasizing D&I initiatives, and paying well.
companyRankingLists.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
Bank of America’s leadership has grown far more diverse in recent years: The board of directors and executive team are more than 50% diverse, and over half the company’s workforce are people of color. Pay equity has also been a priority: In 2023, the company increased its U.S. minimum hourly wage to $23, a step closer to reaching its target of $25 by 2025. Women employees received more than 99% of their male colleagues’ compensation, while employees of color received over 99% of their white coworkers’ compensation. 
 

Bank of America allocated $17 million in tuition assistance in 2022, distributing it to over 5,000 employees. Company policy makes up to $7,500 in educational expenses available to eligible staff every year, through either reimbursement or a prepaid voucher.
 

BofA added a new sabbatical program in 2022, offering workers with 15 years of continuous service four additional weeks of PTO (and up to six weeks for employees who have been with the bank for at least 30 years). By the end of 2023, more than 10,000 staff had taken advantage of the program.

companyRankingLists.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
One of the world’s largest financial institutions, Bank of America serves individual consumers, small and middle-market businesses, and large corporations. Even with more than 170,000 U.S. employees, it still manages to focus on individual career development and mobility.

  • A team of talent mobility specialists serve as a resource to help employees identify new roles within the company, update their résumés, and prep for interviews. Thanks to this program, in 2021, half of the bank’s open roles were filled by internal candidates.

  • BoA raised its minimum wage to $22 in 2022, boosting the annualized salary for full-time employees to over $45,000. Its goal is to further raise wages to $25 by 2025.

  • In 2022, BoA’s employees were provided free lunch from September through November to celebrate their return to the office.

  • For the sixth year, Bank of America awarded over 95% of its employees across the globe with stock awards in addition to their compensation to celebrate the bank’s achievements.

  • “We give teammates many ways to get involved with employee networks and volunteer events,” a Bank of America employee said. “I am proud to work for Bank of America.”

Charlotte-based Bank of America, the second-largest lender in the U.S., had a strong 2022 for the most part, with revenue up 23% over 2021.

  • BofA’s net profit for 2022 was $27.5 billion. That was lower than its 2021 numbers, as higher interest rates ate into margins, but still made the company the eighth most profitable business on this year’s list.

  • The bank’s Merrill wealth management division brought in record revenue of $18.1 billion.

  • Expenses associated with litigation and regulatory investigations in 2022 totaled $1.2 billion, a nearly sixfold increase over 2021. Some of those costs reflected a fine issued by the SEC over the use of unauthorized messaging platforms such as WhatsApp by BofA employees.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: A booming year for banks boosted Bank of America, which saw its stock surge nearly 40% over the course of 2021 as it racked up $22 billion in profit. Rising asset-management and brokerage fees helped grow the bank’s wealth management division’s revenue 16%, to $5.6 billion. companyRankingLists.itemDescription: The financial services giant addressed employee welfare and economic well-being on numerous fronts in 2020. BofA saw through a previous commitment to increase its U.S. minimum hourly wage to $20—doing so a year ahead of schedule. The company made sure to help working parents during a stressful time, providing 3 million days’ worth of backup child and adult care and investing $300 million in care reimbursements for employees. High-risk workers were reassigned to roles they could perform remotely during the pandemic, while BofA continued to pay wages and salaries to those unable to work remotely. And the bank’s employee relief fund provided more than $6 million in grants to those experiencing emergency financial hardships.

companyRankingLists.description: Total revenue for the world’s biggest companies fell 4.8% to $31.7 trillion this year—the first decline in half a decade.
companyRankingLists.title: Fortune Global 500
companyRankingLists.itemDescription: While stock markets raced ahead in 2020, much of the underlying economy continued to struggle. Bank of America, the country’s second largest bank by assets, saw both those dynamics at play in its businesses. Profits dropped 35% to $17.9 billion as the bank put billions on the back burner in preparation for bad loans resulting from the national shutdown. Meanwhile BofA’s investment banking and sales and trading units posted impressive results amid a frenzy of investing activity. And as vaccine rollouts in the U.S. picked up in April, CEO Brian Moynihan struck a far more optimistic tone as the bank released some of those reserves. “What we see different now is…an accelerating recovery versus the economic uncertainty that we would have faced the last year at this time,” he told shareholders, promising an eventual return to the office likely in September.

companyRankingLists.description: As we face unprecedented collective challenges, cooperation has become a business superpower.
companyRankingLists.title: Change the World
companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
Bank of America has loaned $26 billion to pandemic-struck businesses through the Paycheck Protection Program. But some of its most valuable PPP loans were the ones it made through community development financial institutions (CDFIs). CDFIs are nonprofits that combine philanthropic money and private capital to support small businesses whose cash flow or credit histories scare off traditional lenders. This spring, an infusion of more than $250 million in additional credit from BofA, along with $10 million in grants, helped its partner CDFIs keep the doors open at a childcare center in Georgia and a housing and job-training service in Philadelphia, among many other operations. (Pictured at right are two owners of small businesses that partnered with the Community Loan Fund of Chicago, one of BofA's CDFI allies.)


BofA has been building ties with CDFIs for 25 years: It now has a $1.6 billion credit portfolio with 255 CDFI partners across the U.S. It has also stepped up to support minority-owned banks, which often work closely with CDFIs. In early September, BofA announced it would make $50 million in equity investments in so-called minority depository institutions—capital to help them close the racial wealth gap.

companyRankingLists.title: Fortune 500

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
